_arm.bindingCollapse: YES — `--binding-collapse`, and it is the CORRECT mode for this language rather than a leniency: a Clean module is declared in `.dcl` and implemented in `.icl`, so the same member is ONE declaration in two files. The gate's rule collapses a key to ONE declaration iff EVERY declaration answering to it carries the same NON-EMPTY qualifiedName that DIFFERS from the bare name (`qualifiedName = name` is the store's file-scope fallback, and a fallback is not a qualification). MEASURED 2026-10-29: **3,148 keys collapsed** (719 on 2026-10-28), 7,836 qualifiedName aliases indexed (2,649), and the growth is the module-qualified identity fix below — a module-level `.dcl`/`.icl` pair could not collapse before it, because the analyzer published no qualifiedName at module scope at all. `references` ambiguity 1,808 -> 1,011 and `exports` 40 -> 12 come from that fix; `overrides` was 2/306 -> 306/306 on 2026-10-28 (the class-member half of the same pair, whose `Owner.member` spelling already qualified).

closure._external_is_a_coarsening: `external` HERE = externalVerified + binding-verified FILE claims: 891 `imports` (574 confirmed `importProjectFile` claims + 317 confirmed `moduleNamespace` claims) + 3,843 verified `references` `isStdlib` claims + 4 verified `implements` claims (`FileEnv`/`FileSystem`, the stdlib class names, verified through their owner). Every one is a CLAIM and none is a resolution, so the lane's coarsening covers them. `extFAIL` is 0 and `ext?` is 0.

module-halves-are-one-module.ruling: The target is a MODULE name and EVERY declaration answering it is a MODULE symbol: the `.dcl` half (`definition module X`) and the `.icl` half (`implementation module X`) of ONE module. A target that names a module cannot be ambiguous by MEANING — Clean has one module per name, and these two are it — but the gate's collapse cannot merge the key, because its rule requires a qualifiedName that DIFFERS from the bare name and a module's qualified identity IS its name (`qualifiedName = name`, which is the store's fallback spelling and must not be read as a qualification). MEASURED on the arm's own dump with the census covering the whole population: 590 rows, top targets `Cocoa.objc` 30 · `UtilStrictLists` 27 · `StdClass` 26 · `Cocoa.Foundation` 22 · `Cocoa.msg` 21 · `StdOverloaded` 20, all of them two module symbols. NOT COUNTED AS A DEFECT OF THE ANALYZER: publishing the module from both halves is TRUE (both files declare it), and suppressing one half would be a false statement made to move a number. This is a GATE-MODEL limit, named and priced.

falsifier.wouldFail: a `references` row in the module-halves bucket whose declaration set contains anything other than MODULE symbols, or a module in the corpus whose `.dcl` and `.icl` halves do NOT both publish the module symbol (then the twin is not the cause).

module-name-reused-as-a-type.ruling: A MODULE symbol plus a NON-module declaration of the same name: Clean projects name their central type after the module, so `Diagnostic.icl` declares `Diagnostic` (type) in the same project whose module symbol is also `Diagnostic`. The module's own name is not a collapsible gap (see the ruling above) and the type is a real declaration, so a type position answers both. MEASURED: 95 rows, `Diagnostic` 46 · `Range` 23 · `Symbol` 14 · `Target` 8 · `typewin` 2 · `logfile` 1 — and the declaration sets are exactly (module symbol + the module's own type). The analyzer cannot drop either: the type is what the reference means, and the module symbol is what `contains`/`exports` edges use as their source.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose non-module declarations are NOT declared by the same module whose module symbol answers the name (then it is cross-module, not the module/type idiom).

module-level-same-name-in-different-modu.ruling: Two or more MODULE-LEVEL declarations of the same name in DIFFERENT modules of one project — the module-qualified identity distinguishes them (that is why they did NOT collapse), and a bare target genuinely means one of several. `List` 164 (a FUNCTION `List` in Clyde's `UtilOptions` and a TYPE `List` in `UtilStrictLists`, so the kinds differ as well) and `NSView` 13 (`Cocoa.layout` and `Cocoa.tabview` each declare the type). This is the one residual class where the name really is overloaded at module scope, and it is a property of the corpus rather than of the analyzer: the source writes a bare name and the language resolves it by the import's module, which a name-keyed arbiter does not model. NOT FIXED, COUNTED — a fix would mean a qualified target spelling the source does not write.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose module-level declarations all share ONE module (i.e. a `.dcl`/`.icl` twin the qualified identity failed to collapse) — the census reports that as `twin-not-collapsed`, and its count is 0.

class-name-is-its-members-name.ruling: One CLASS/INTERFACE declaration plus N members that spell the class's OWN name — Clean's degenerate naming: `class toString a` declares `toString`, and EVERY instance of it declares a member `toString`, so the bare key answers the class AND every instance's member. MEASURED **132** rows REMAINING after the class-like rule (313 before it): references 104 · implements 15 · calls 3 · exports 10. A NAME-keyed key space cannot pick the class out of that set; a KIND-aware one can, and THE CLASS-LIKE RULE NOW DOES for `implements` rows (TAKEN 2026-10-29, `implementsClassLike` in the classifier): it took 181 of this bucket's 196 `implements` rows. The 104 `references`, 3 `calls` and 10 `exports` rows remain because their LABEL does not say the target is a class — a `references` row may name a value. The analyzer emits the right target — the instance names its class — so this is a RULING ABOUT THE MODEL, not a target-spelling defect. It is the same family the `overrides` caveat named on 2026-10-28 (`addTabViewItem.addTabViewItem`), now measured for every type.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket with NO class/interface declaration among its declarations (the census would place it in `instance-member-collision`), or a class whose members do NOT share its name (then the target could resolve and the row is a defect, not the idiom).

instance-members-without-the-class.ruling: Every declaration answering the target is a MEMBER (ownerName is a type), in two or more owners, and NO class declaration answers it. For an `implements` row this is the OPERATOR-CLASS SPELLING effect, measured: the class is DECLARED parenthesised (`class (<<<) a` in clean-stdlib/StdFile.dcl) while the INSTANCE spells it bare (`instance <<< ...`), so the bare target answers only the instances' same-named members (`<<<` 24, `<` 31, `==` 18, `%` 16, `+` 9, `-` 9). MEASURED 181 rows, and the alternative was PRICED rather than waved away: 198 of the 769 `implements` targets are operator-shaped, and **153 of the 333 ambiguous rows name a class that IS declared parenthesised in the edge's own project** — so publishing the declaration's spelling `(<class>)` would resolve 153. It is NOT taken, for two reasons that are both facts and not preferences: (1) the lane's own identity for an operator class is the BARE name — `isLocallyDeclaredOperatorClass` reads `(<class>)` as the DECLARATION's spelling and matches the instance's bare name to it — so a parenthesised TARGET asserts a spelling the source does not write in that position; (2) the 153 are clean-stdlib's own declared-here rows, and the other 180 would move from ambiguous to unresolved, i.e. the same wall with a different label, which is exactly the kind of label move the contract forbids when it is presented as progress. Recorded as a MEASURED DESIGN DECISION, decision (a) of two. LATER THE SAME DAY, THE LEVER WAS PRICED THE OTHER WAY, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT LEVER: a GATE-SIDE rule that leaves the ANALYZER's target spelling exactly as the source writes it and resolves the row against the CLASS among the key's declarations. `validation/m14/fixtures/clean/implements-class-spelling.mts` (the arm's own `--dump` + the project's own symbols over `git ls-files`, 333 ambiguous rows, 333 classified) measures the split: **153** decided by the PARENTHESISED spelling (`(T)` is declared class-like and collapses to one — `(==)` 43, `(<)` 31, `(<<<)` 24, `(%)` 16, …), **131** decided by the BARE spelling (`T` is itself the class and collapses to one — `~` 7 proves the spelling is a project fact and NOT derivable per file, `fromString` 13, `toInt` 8, …), and **49** with no class-like declaration under EITHER spelling — split by measurement into **47** whose class is declared in ANOTHER project of the corpus (Clyde's `instance == Processor` names `StdOverloaded`'s class, declared in `clean-stdlib`) and **2** declared NOWHERE in the corpus (`JSONEncode`/`JSONDecode`, eastwood `SemVer.dcl:38-39`). So the analyzer-side rewrite's cost was real (the 180 would have moved ambiguous -> unresolved) and the gate-side rule has no such cost. TAKEN 2026-10-29: `implementsClassLike` in `script/m14/incoming-gate.ts` plus the `classLike` branch in `incoming-rule.ts` resolve the row against the key's CLASS-LIKE declarations under the bare, then the parenthesised, spelling, requiring ONE qualified identity. MEASURED ON THE ARM: **284 rows resolved, exactly the price** — `implements` 417 -> **701** resolved, ambiguous 333 -> **49**; overall resolved 21,791 -> **22,075**, ambiguous 1,360 -> **1,076**, every other column unchanged, extFAIL still 0 — and THIS bucket 181 -> **78** (`implements` 135 -> 32). The analyzer is UNCHANGED: the rule is in the classifier.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose class-like declarations DO carry exactly one qualified identity (then `implementsClassLike` should have taken it), or a row the rule took whose class-like declarations carry two DISTINCT qualifiedNames (then it resolved to one of two classes). Re-run the arm and compare the bucket counts with 78 / 32.

import-module-file-on-a-search-path.ruling: The target is a `Module:item` / `Module:*` import whose MODULE the edge's own project DECLARES, but whose FILE the claim's candidate spellings did not reach: Clean modules are found on a SEARCH PATH, not at the project root (`UtilStrictLists` lives at `cleantools/Util/UtilStrictLists.icl`, not beside `Clyde/outlineviewcontroller.icl` that imports it). MEASURED 222 rows, `UtilStrictLists:*` 18 · `StdPathname:*` 12 · `Range:*` 10 · `Diagnostic:Diagnostic` 9 · `UtilStrictLists:List` 7. THE CLAIM IS NOT MADE, DELIBERATELY: an unconfirmed file claim REFUTES (`extFAIL`), and a project-wide search is the only spelling that would confirm these — priced at 243 edges (`imports-claim-pricing.mts`, candidate set C, every hit a file that DECLARES the module; its leaf-ambiguity question WAS settled by a follow-up probe — 239 unique-directory hits and 4 for eastwood's two `Linter.icl` files), but not taken, for a reason that is soundness rather than cost: the claim is checked against the ADMITTED list (`git ls-files`), and a filesystem walk can name an UNTRACKED file (a `_build` copy) that the gate would REFUTE. MEASURED 2026-10-29: `git ls-files --others` for `*.icl`/`*.dcl` is 0 in all five repositories, so a walk would be sound on THIS corpus — but the admitted list is exactly what a per-file analyzer does not have, and production Clean trees carry untracked `_build` output. The performance cost is a second, unmeasured limit (the lane has no `Clyde:clean` F baseline row to charge it to). PROPOSED, NOT CLAIMED: `validation/m14/proposals/clean-import-file-claim-project-search.md`.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose module is NOT declared by the edge's project (then it belongs to another bucket), or a candidate-set-C hit whose file does not declare the module.

falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose module is ALSO declared by the edge's own project (then the file claim should have been reachable) or declared by NO project (then it belongs in `import-module-declared-nowhere`).

import-module-declared-nowhere.ruling: The import names a module NO admitted file declares anywhere in the corpus — the Clean platform libraries the corpus does not carry: `Data.Error:*` 22 · `Data.Maybe:*` 21 · `Text:*` 20 · `System._Pointer:*` 14 · `System.FilePath:*` 14 · `System.File:*` 14. A claim COULD be manufactured here (`moduleNamespace` verifies whenever the project does not carry the module) and that is exactly why it is refused — the closed stdlib list is the evidence and these modules are not in it (the corpus's `clean-stdlib` carries only the `Std*` modules; `Data/` and `System/` are absent, measured by `stdlib-inventory.mts`). falsifier.wouldFail: a module in this bucket declared by any admitted file in the corpus (the inventory walks clean-stdlib and Prelude through production `parseFile`), or a `Data.*`/`System.*` module file present in `clean-stdlib` after all.

reference-module-in-another-project.ruling: A `references` row that names a MODULE the corpus carries in another project — `Data.List` 15 · `Data.Functor` 15 · `Control.Monad` 10 · `Control.Applicative` 6 · `Data.Array` 3 · `Data.Bool` 2. falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose module the edge's OWN project declares, or one declared nowhere (a different class).

reference-symbol-in-another-project.ruling: The target is a bare NAME declared by another project of the corpus and not by the edge's: `Map` 15 · `JSONDecode` 4 · `ProcessHandle` 4 · `JSONEncode` 2 · `fromString` 2 · `FileInfo` 2. falsifier.wouldFail: a row in this bucket whose name is declared by the edge's own project (then it is an analyzer defect, not a boundary) or by no project at all.

name-declared-nowhere-in-the-corpus.ruling: The target is declared by NO admitted file in any project. Three sub-classes, each measured, and NONE is a candidate for a claim: (1) the Clean platform's own names whose StdEnv declaration is not in the corpus at all — `Pointer` 238 · `Property` 117 · `FilePath` 63 · `MaybeError` 33 · `System.FilePath` 30 · `Text` 27 · `Data.Maybe` 24 · `Data.Func` 22 — and `clean-stdlib/_system.dcl`, which is where StdEnv declares them, is a 0-byte file in this checkout (the arm lists it among its 3 empty results); (2) DOTTED calls into platform modules (`Data.Error.Ok` 11 · `Data.Map.get` 10 · `Data.Map.toList` 6 · `Data.Map.put` 5), i.e. a qualified call whose module is absent; (3) derived-generic members of an external class (`gLSPJSONDecode` 4 · `ConstructFromYAML` 2 · `gLSPJSONEncode` 2 · `gLexOrd` 1 · `ggen` 1). THE STDLIB-LIST EXTENSION WAS PROBED AND REFUSED on 2026-10-28: `clean-stdlib` and `Prelude` are in the corpus (74 + 42 files) and **0 of the 10 most frequent unresolved targets are declared in them**, so widening the closed list would be a vocabulary rather than evidence. ★ THE IMPORT CLAIM WAS THE LANE'S FALSE STATEMENT AND IS CORRECTED (2026-10-29). The 2026-10-28 declaration recorded `imports` as 1,932 answered with `extFAIL 0`; the SAME arm reads extFAIL **1,177** and the verified total is 891 (574 `importProjectFile` + 317 `moduleNamespace`), not 1,932. The 1,177 were `importProjectFile` arrays emitted for EVERY non-stdlib module at the two import sites, without the shared guard — a file claim is a statement the project can REFUTE, and the project refuted 1,177 of them (a Clean module's file is on a search path, not at the root the candidate arithmetic spelled). FIXED AT THE SOURCE: the emission sites no longer state the claim; PASS 3 states it only where `fileClaimForTarget` CONFIRMS a candidate on disk, from the importing file's own directory first and the project root second (the pricing instrument measured 438 + 136 = 574 such files, every one a file that DECLARES the module). extFAIL is 0 and ext? is 0.

★ THE MODULE-QUALIFIED IDENTITY IS THE ROUND'S FIX (2026-10-29): every MODULE-LEVEL symbol now publishes `Module.name` (`StdPathname.Pathname`, `PmTypes.Project`), where it published none. A module-level type/function/class/macro is ONE declaration written in BOTH halves of a Clean module, and the gate's collapse could not see the pair because a collision needs a qualifiedName that differs from the bare name. MEASURED, whole population, BEFORE -> AFTER on the same arm: `references` ambiguous 1,808 -> 1,011 (-797, exactly the collapse price measured beforehand by `validation/m14/fixtures/clean/collapse-price.mts` over the gate's own dump), `exports` 40 -> 12 (-28), `calls` unresolved 75 -> 74, resolved 20,958 -> 21,791 (+833), collapsed keys 719 -> 3,148. THE EXCLUSIONS ARE THE CONTRACT: a MEMBER keeps its owner's spelling (`Sized.sizeOf`), which is what `overrides`/`implements` endpoints are written in; a LOCAL keeps its frame-scoped spelling; a MODULE symbol keeps its name (there is nothing above a module). ONE over-collapse was priced and accepted: the only same-module cross-kind pairs the collapse merges are 4 GENERICS and their case functions (`bimap`, `binumap`, `gEqTest`, `exampleGeneric`) — one entity, not two.

★ THE POPULATION'S REPOSITORIES ARE NOW RECORDED (2026-10-29): 312 files over 5 repositories — clean-stdlib 74, Prelude 42, Clyde 109, eastwood 73, cloogle.org 14. The 2026-10-28 declaration recorded this as OWED (`meta.repos` absent); it is closed here. The corpus ALSO carries the Clean platform library sources `Prelude` (Data.*, Control.*, Text.Show, System.IO) and `clean-stdlib` (Std*), which is why so many rows in the classes above name a module the corpus holds in a DIFFERENT project — the per-project scope is production's, and those rows are the price of it.

★ THE PHANTOM CLASS IS CLOSED AND THE AMBIGUITY THAT REPLACED IT IS NOT A PHANTOM ONE (2026-10-28, re-measured 2026-10-29): the instance containers are namespaced (`<target>::instance`, kind `impl`), 0 `onlyPhantom` and 0 `oneRealPlusPhantom` in `phantom-census.mts`. ★ `extends` IS RULED GRAMMAR-ABSENCE, MEASURED (2026-10-28): `validation/m14/measurements/clean-grammar-nodes.json` enumerates the SERVED wasm — **143 named types over 290 ids, and 0 of them match extend|inherit|subclass|superclass**. Clean's composition constructs are type classes and instances (`class_declaration`, `class_member`, `instance_class`) plus `derive_declaration`, all of which publish `implements`, not `extends`. The suite's zero `extends` edges over 312 files is therefore a property of the LANGUAGE, not a silence of the analyzer.

MEASURED: exports 4,596 -> **4,303** edges (293 spurious self-exports removed), ambiguity 162 -> **40**, resolved 4,434 -> 4,263 — the 171 'resolved' rows lost were the same degenerate self-edges, which is the correct direction: an edge that says a module exports itself is false whether it binds or not. (After the 2026-10-29 module-qualified identity fix the exports row reads 4,291 resolved / 12 ambiguous.)
